name: Courage
definition: You are vulnerable in search for the truth; you are willing to risk failure, or challenge the status quo, in the pursuit of excellence.

rows.situation: A question you cannot answer yet
rows.justRight: Says what you do not know and what you will do to find out.
rows.over: Announces your uncertainty so often that people cannot tell when you actually have a view.

rows.situation: A course that could fail in public and might be excellent
rows.under: Picks the safe version so a failure cannot be tied to you.
rows.justRight: Takes the bet when the upside is real, names the failure mode, and learns from it if it misses.
rows.over: Seeks public risk for its own sake, including bets that were never aimed at a better result.

rows.situation: A settled practice that is getting in the way of excellent work
rows.under: Leaves it alone because it is how things are done.
rows.justRight: Challenges it with a specific case, and stays to help replace it if you were right.
rows.over: Attacks every settled practice, including the ones that are why the work is good.

rows.situation: A hard truth about the work that requires you to look bad first
rows.under: Protects your image and lets the team keep the wrong story.
rows.justRight: Puts the unflattering fact on the table so the team can decide from it.
rows.over: Shares personal discomfort that does not help the decision, and calls that courage.

rows.situation: Disagreeing with someone who can affect your job
rows.under: Agrees in the room and complains later.
rows.justRight: Says the disagreement in the room, about the work, and accepts the decision once it is made.
rows.over: Picks fights with senior people to be seen as brave, including on things that do not matter.
